usage: A common everyday noun for a pair of shears or scissors; in gardening, it often means pruning shears.
Use it with measure words like 一把剪刀 when counting or asking for one pair of shears.
Very natural in home, school, and garden contexts; for bigger garden tools, people may also say 剪枝鉸.
In speech, it is a very basic, high-frequency word, so it is fine for beginner Cantonese.
